content.comment_body: Hello, I'm facing an issue where I can upload a program via ethernet, but when attempting to do so with a microSD card, the [product_name] reports that the card is empty. It's a new 32GB card formatted as FAT32. I've followed the instructions from the user manual and saved the program as .bin using the Save As function in [product_name] software, with only the LOGO_U_P.bin file on the card. Is there any specific formatting required for this SD card besides the default settings? Thanks.

Which operating system did you use to format the SD card? Does your [product_name] have a display? If so, have you checked the SD card diagnostics? Does the [product_name] recognize the SD card? Please specify the exact hardware and provide the order number.

Which operating system did you use to format the SD card? Does your [product_name] have a display? If so, have you checked the SD card diagnostics? Is the SD card recognized by the [product_name]? Please specify the exact model and provide the order number.

I used Windows 10 Pro for formatting. My [product_name] (order no. [article_no]) has a display. The diagnostics indicate the card is "OK". It appears to transfer correctly, but says the program is empty when I try to start. Opening the .bin from the SD card in [product_name] software displays the expected function block diagram.

Try deleting the file from the SD card. Insert the empty, formatted card into the [product_name]. Transfer the program in [product_name] and ensure that 'Copy to SD card' is checked in the transfer window. Then delete the program from the [product_name], power off, and power on again. Check if the [product_name] successfully loads the program from the SD card.

It seems that if the [product_name] saves the program to the card, both the device and PC can read it. Saving to the card via [product_name] software while the card is in the device works. However, if the PC writes the .bin file to the card, the [product_name] sees it as empty. So, it's not possible to save the .bin from the PC and load it using the SD card.

Yes, but this isn't an issue with [product_name] or its software, it's a Windows problem. Sometimes, Windows 10/11 FAT32 formatting isn't completely compatible. When I format SD cards using Windows 7, there are no issues.

Thanks for your support. I managed to resolve the issue by formatting the SD card using command prompt as an administrator: format FS:FAT32 E:. The system manual also states exFAT support is expected, and the product details say it accepts a standard microSD card, but FAT32 formatting seems required despite it not being the current standard.
Currently, starting with [product_name] [version_no], both FAT32 and exFAT formatting are supported.

[product_name] software can read from and write to cards formatted as exFAT. However, after formatting to exFAT using Command Prompt (same method as for FAT32), the [product_name] device can't recognize the card as a valid SD card. That's the root of the problem.
Can you explain how you transfer your program to the SD card? If the card diagnostics on the [product_name] report the card is OK, our experience suggests the card should work fine.

Hello, returning to this discussion because I'm updating the [product_name] using a microSD card—formatted to FAT32 and empty. I save the .bin file straight to the card using 'Save As' in [product_name] software, version [version_no], without renaming it (LOGO_U_P.bin). After safely ejecting the card and placing it into the powered-off [product_name], powering on, I go to the menu, select Card > Load Program, and confirm. The device pretends to load, but starting gives 'Error: Empty Program.' Checking the card on the PC shows the .bin file and a _dirmeta.dat file. Opening the .bin in [product_name] software looks correct, so it's not a card error.
What does the display on your [product_name] show under diagnostics when you insert the SD card?

Hello, which [product_name] hardware are you selecting in [product_name] software when storing the program to the SD card? What is the order number and firmware version of your device? Did you save the file in the root directory of the SD card?

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter inconsistent results when uploading programs to the [product_name] controller using a microSD card. The device reliably reads and writes to FAT32-formatted cards when formatted with specific tools, but fails with files saved by the PC or when formatted as exFAT or via standard Windows 10 formatting. Formatting and managing the card with the [product_name] device itself works as intended, causing confusion about supported file systems and reliable workflows.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] controller to recognize and load a .bin program file from a microSD card formatted on a Windows 10 PC, either as FAT32 or exFAT, in accordance with the procedures outlined in the manual.
